CHAPTER 1.3 · LEARNING AREA 1

CHAPTER 1.3 · LEARNING AREA 1 · OCTOBER · NOVEMBER

Laws of arithmetic, equations and word problems

Two people work out the same calculation and get different results. Who is right? The order of operations decides. With the laws of arithmetic you save work, with equations you solve number puzzles, and with a plan you crack word problems where at first you do not even know where to start.

10 LESSONS3 UNITS2 LABS
WHAT YOU WILL LEARN IN THIS CHAPTER
  • follow the order of operations, also on the calculator
  • calculate cleverly by swapping, grouping and distributing
  • solve equations and inequalities by reasoning, working backwards and trying
  • work on word problems with a plan and check the result

$12 - 5 = 7$

$\tfrac24 + \tfrac14 = \tfrac34$

UNIT 14 LESSONS

1Laws of arithmetic and order of operations

Ben is right. He first calculated $\tfrac13 \cdot \tfrac34 = \tfrac14$ and then $\tfrac12 + \tfrac14 = \tfrac34$. Ana added first. So that everyone gets the same result, there is a fixed order of operations. It applies to fractions and decimals just as to natural numbers.

You already know the laws of arithmetic too. They still hold and help you calculate cleverly. The calculator knows the order of operations as well: it is built in. If you type $2 + 3 \cdot 4$, it shows $14$.

KEY POINT · ORDER AND LAWS

Order: 1. brackets   2. multiplication and division ($\cdot$ and $:$)   3. addition and subtraction ($+$ and $-$). Otherwise from left to right.

Swapping (commutative law): $a + b = b + a$   and   $a \cdot b = b \cdot a$

Grouping (associative law): $(a + b) + c = a + (b + c)$   and   $(a \cdot b) \cdot c = a \cdot (b \cdot c)$

Distributing (distributive law): $a \cdot (b + c) = a \cdot b + a \cdot c$

Careful with minus and divide: here you may not swap. $5 - 2$ is not $2 - 5$, and $6 : 3$ is not $3 : 6$.

Fractions in the calculator: with the fraction key or in brackets: $(3 : 4)$.

INTERACTIVE · STEP BY STEP

What comes next is underlined. Choose a calculation and tap “Next step”.

EXAMPLE 1 · SWAPPING AND GROUPING

Calculate cleverly: $0.25 \cdot 7.3 \cdot 4$.

Swap and group: $(0.25 \cdot 4) \cdot 7.3 = 1 \cdot 7.3$.

$7.3$, without any written calculation at all.

EXAMPLE 2 · DISTRIBUTING

Calculate cleverly: $\tfrac35 \cdot 4 + \tfrac35 \cdot 6$.

Both products have the factor $\tfrac35$: $\tfrac35 \cdot (4 + 6) = \tfrac35 \cdot 10$.

$6$

EXERCISES

a) $\tfrac12 + \tfrac12 \cdot \tfrac12$   b) $\left(\tfrac12 + \tfrac12\right) \cdot \tfrac12$   c) $2 - 0.5 \cdot 2$   d) $6 : \tfrac12 + 1$   e) $0.3 + 0.7 \cdot 10$

a) $\tfrac34$   b) $\tfrac12$   c) $1$   d) $12 + 1 = 13$   e) $0.3 + 7 = 7.3$

Calculate cleverly: a) $\tfrac27 + \tfrac34 + \tfrac57$   b) $0.5 \cdot 3.9 \cdot 2$   c) $1.25 \cdot 0.3 \cdot 8$   d) $\tfrac49 \cdot 7 + \tfrac49 \cdot 2$

a) $\left(\tfrac27 + \tfrac57\right) + \tfrac34 = 1\tfrac34$   b) $3.9$   c) $(1.25 \cdot 8) \cdot 0.3 = 10 \cdot 0.3 = 3$   d) $\tfrac49 \cdot 9 = 4$

Put in brackets so that the calculation is right: a) $\tfrac12 + \tfrac14 \cdot 4 = 3$   b) $3 - 1 : \tfrac12 = 4$   c) $0.2 + 0.3 \cdot 0.5 + 0.5 = 0.5$

a) $\left(\tfrac12 + \tfrac14\right) \cdot 4 = 3$   b) $(3 - 1) : \tfrac12 = 4$   c) $(0.2 + 0.3) \cdot (0.5 + 0.5) = 0.5$

CALCCalculate with the calculator: the sum of $3.6$ and $2.4$ is to be divided by $1.5$. What do you have to type in? What comes out without brackets?

$(3.6 + 2.4) : 1.5 = 4$. Without brackets the calculator works out $3.6 + 2.4 : 1.5 = 3.6 + 1.6 = 5.2$.

Tim calculates: $\tfrac34 \cdot \left(8 + \tfrac13\right) = 6 + \tfrac13$. Find his mistake and calculate correctly.

When distributing, each term is multiplied by $\tfrac34$.

Tim only multiplied the 8 by $\tfrac34$. Correct: $\tfrac34 \cdot 8 + \tfrac34 \cdot \tfrac13 = 6 + \tfrac14 = 6\tfrac14$.

TEST YOURSELF!

$\tfrac12 + \tfrac12 \cdot \tfrac13 = \;?$

$\tfrac12 + \tfrac16 = \tfrac46 = \tfrac23$

$0.25 \cdot 3.7 \cdot 4 = \;?$

$(0.25 \cdot 4) \cdot 3.7 = 3.7$

$\left(\tfrac23 + \tfrac16\right) \cdot 6 = \;?$

$\tfrac23 \cdot 6 + \tfrac16 \cdot 6 = 4 + 1 = 5$

UNIT 24 LESSONS

2Equations and inequalities

“I think of a number $a$. I multiply it by $\tfrac95$ and get 1.” As an equation: $\tfrac95 \cdot a = 1$. Working backwards: $a = 1 : \tfrac95 = \tfrac59$. Check: $\tfrac95 \cdot \tfrac59 = \tfrac{45}{45} = 1$ ✓

An equation contains a variable, a letter standing for an unknown number. A solution is a number that gives a true statement when substituted. In Year 6 you solve equations by reasoning:

  • Working backwards with the inverse operation: $x + \tfrac34 = 2$ becomes $x = 2 - \tfrac34 = \tfrac54$.
  • Trying: substitute values, compare, record them in a table.
  • At the end, always check.

An inequality such as $4 \cdot x < 3$ usually has many solutions. Among the fractional numbers there are even infinitely many: all numbers less than $\tfrac34$.

KEY POINT · SOLVING EQUATIONS BY REASONING

Plus and minus, times and divided by are inverse operations of each other:

$x + a = b \;\Rightarrow\; x = b - a$   ·   $x - a = b \;\Rightarrow\; x = b + a$

$a \cdot x = b \;\Rightarrow\; x = b : a$   ·   $x : a = b \;\Rightarrow\; x = b \cdot a$

Check: substitute the solution. If a true statement comes out, it is right.

Divisor wanted: for $12 : v = 3$ you ask: “By what do I have to divide 12 to get 3?” So $v = 12 : 3 = 4$.

Inequality: $<$ means “less than”, $>$ means “greater than”, $\leq$ means “less than or equal to”.

INTERACTIVE · SUBSTITUTING AND COMPARING

Move the slider to substitute numbers. Green points on the number line fit, red ones do not.

EXAMPLE 3 · WORKING BACKWARDS

Solve $0.6 \cdot y = 4.2$ and $x - \tfrac13 = \tfrac12$.

$y = 4.2 : 0.6 = 42 : 6 = 7$. Check: $0.6 \cdot 7 = 4.2$ ✓

$x = \tfrac12 + \tfrac13 = \tfrac56$. Check: $\tfrac56 - \tfrac26 = \tfrac36 = \tfrac12$ ✓   $y = 7$, $x = \tfrac56$

EXAMPLE 4 · AN INEQUALITY

Which natural numbers satisfy $x + 0.5 < 2$? Which fractional numbers?

$x + 0.5 = 2$ holds for $x = 1.5$. $x$ must be smaller.

natural numbers: 0 and 1. Fractional numbers: all from 0 to just under $1.5$, for example $1.49$.

EXERCISES

Solve and check: a) $x + \tfrac25 = 1$   b) $y - 0.7 = 1.3$   c) $3 \cdot z = 2$   d) $a : 4 = 0.5$   e) $\tfrac12 \cdot b = \tfrac38$

a) $\tfrac35$   b) $2$   c) $\tfrac23$   d) $2$   e) $\tfrac38 : \tfrac12 = \tfrac34$

Give all natural numbers that satisfy the inequality: a) $x + 3 < 7$   b) $2 \cdot x \leq 9$   c) $10 : x > 4$

In c) $x$ must not be 0.

a) $\{0, 1, 2, 3\}$   b) $\{0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}$   c) $\{1, 2\}$, because $10 : 2 = 5 > 4$, but $10 : 3 = 3.\overline{3}$

Write as an equation and solve: “If I add $\tfrac23$ to a number, I get double $\tfrac56$.”

$x + \tfrac23 = 2 \cdot \tfrac56 = \tfrac53$, so $x = \tfrac53 - \tfrac23 = 1$.

Solve by reasoning: a) $\tfrac{14}{v} = \tfrac72$   b) $\tfrac34 \cdot x < \tfrac34$   c) $1.2 : w = 0.4$

a) $\tfrac{14}{4} = \tfrac72$, so $v = 4$   b) all $x$ less than 1   c) $w = 1.2 : 0.4 = 3$

Give three fractional numbers that satisfy $0.5 < x < 0.6$. How many are there altogether? How many natural numbers satisfy the inequality?

For example $0.51$, $0.55$, $\tfrac{4}{7} \approx 0.57$. There are infinitely many, because between two fractional numbers there is always another one. Natural numbers: none.

TEST YOURSELF!

$\tfrac23 \cdot x = 1$. What is $x$?

$x = 1 : \tfrac23 = \tfrac32$

$x - 1.25 = 0.75$. What is $x$?

$x = 0.75 + 1.25 = 2$

How many natural numbers satisfy $3 \cdot x < 10$?

$0, 1, 2, 3$: four numbers. $3 \cdot 4 = 12$ is too big.

UNIT 32 LESSONS

3Word problems with a plan

Draw the class as a strip. $\tfrac38$ cycle and $\tfrac14 = \tfrac28$ take the bus; together that is $\tfrac58$. That leaves $\tfrac38$ for the walkers, and that is 9 people. So $\tfrac18$ of the class is 3 people, and the whole class has $8 \cdot 3 = 24$.

With a fixed plan you do not get lost in a long problem. A sketch or a table shows what you know and what is missing. For the quantity you want you can introduce a variable and set up an equation. At the end you check whether the result fits the situation.

KEY POINT · A PLAN FOR SOLVING
  1. Understand: what is given, what is wanted? Say it in your own words.
  2. Represent: a sketch, a strip or a table. Introduce a variable if needed.
  3. Calculate: set up an equation or calculate step by step; trying is allowed too.
  4. Check and answer: does the result fit? Write a sentence as your answer.

Does it fit? A class with $23.5$ people or a journey to school of 400 km cannot be right. Then you look for the mistake.

Units: calculate everything in the same unit, for example everything in grams or everything in kilograms.

EXAMPLE 5 · WITH A STRIP AND AN EQUATION

Ali gets a third of the marbles, Bea a quarter. Carl gets the rest, which is 15 marbles. How many marbles were there?

Rest: $1 - \tfrac13 - \tfrac14 = \tfrac{12}{12} - \tfrac{4}{12} - \tfrac{3}{12} = \tfrac{5}{12}$. With $m$ for all the marbles: $\tfrac{5}{12} \cdot m = 15$.

$m = 15 : \tfrac{5}{12} = 15 \cdot \tfrac{12}{5} = 36$. Check: $12 + 9 + 15 = 36$ ✓   There were 36 marbles.

EXAMPLE 6 · WITH A TABLE

Lea has already saved €12.50 and adds €2.50 every week. When will she have €40 for a skateboard?

Weeks0481011
Savings in €12.5022.5032.5037.5040.00

€27.50 is missing, and $27.50 : 2.50 = 11$. After 11 weeks.

EXERCISES

A cake is cut into 12 pieces. Mia eats a quarter of the cake, Tom a third. How many pieces are left?

Mia: $\tfrac14 \cdot 12 = 3$, Tom: $\tfrac13 \cdot 12 = 4$. $12 - 3 - 4 = 5$ pieces are left.

A hiking trail is $12.6$ km long. After $\tfrac23$ of the way the class takes a break. How far is it still?

$\tfrac13$ of the way is missing: $12.6 : 3 = 4.2$ km.

For a class party you buy $4.5$ kg of apples at €2.40 per kilogram and 3 bottles of juice at €1.35 each. You pay with a €20 note. How much change do you get?

Apples: $4.5 \cdot 2.40 = 10.80$ €. Juice: $3 \cdot 1.35 = 4.05$ €. Together €14.85. Change: €5.15.

A glass of juice weighs 450 g. When the glass is half full, it weighs 290 g. How heavy is the empty glass?

The difference is exactly half the juice.

Half the juice weighs $450 - 290 = 160$ g, all the juice 320 g. The glass weighs $450 - 320 = 130$ g. Check: $130 + 160 = 290$ ✓

TEST YOURSELF!

$\tfrac38$ of a class cycle, $\tfrac14$ take the bus, the other 9 walk. How many are in the class?

$\tfrac38$ of the class are 9, so $\tfrac18$ is 3 and the class has 24.

How much change do you get from €20 if you have to pay €14.85?

$20 - 14.85 = 5.15$

REVIEW · DEEPEN · CONNECT

Calculate: a) $\tfrac23 \cdot \left(\tfrac34 - \tfrac14\right)$   b) $1.5 + 2.5 \cdot 0.4$   c) $\left(1 - \tfrac15\right) : \tfrac25$

a) $\tfrac23 \cdot \tfrac12 = \tfrac13$   b) $1.5 + 1 = 2.5$   c) $\tfrac45 : \tfrac25 = 2$

Mind reading from the exploration: “times 2, plus 3, times 5” gives 65. Which number was it? And if 52.5 comes out?

Backwards: $65 : 5 = 13$, $13 - 3 = 10$, $10 : 2 = 5$. For $52.5$: $10.5 - 3 = 7.5$, $7.5 : 2 = 3.75$.

Connecting with chapter 1.1: a jacket costs €60. In the end-of-season sale there is $25\%$ off. What does it cost then?

$25\% = \tfrac14$. Discount: $\tfrac14 \cdot 60 = 15$ €. New price: €45.

A snail climbs up a wall 3 m high. During the day it manages $0.6$ m, at night it slides back $0.4$ m. On which day does it reach the top?

Careful: on the last day it does not slide back any more. Make a table.

Each day and night it gets $0.2$ m higher. After 12 days and nights it is at $2.4$ m. On the 13th day it climbs $0.6$ m and is at the top.

EXCURSIONA FAMOUS PUZZLE

The 35 camels

🐪 Three brothers are quarrelling in the desert. Their father has left them 35 camels. The eldest is to get half, the middle one a third, the youngest a ninth. But 35 cannot be divided by 2, by 3 or by 9.

A traveller who is good at arithmetic gives the brothers his own camel. Now there are 36. The eldest gets 18, the middle one 12, the youngest 4. Everyone gets more than was due to him and is happy. Together that is 34 camels. Two are left over: the traveller gets one back and keeps the other as his reward.

How can that be? Work out $\tfrac12 + \tfrac13 + \tfrac19$. What do you notice?

$\tfrac12 + \tfrac13 + \tfrac19 = \tfrac{9}{18} + \tfrac{6}{18} + \tfrac{2}{18} = \tfrac{17}{18}$. The father did not share out all the camels! One eighteenth was left over. Of 36 camels that is exactly 2. And because $35 \cdot \tfrac{17}{18}$ is less than 34, each brother gets a little more than his share of 35.

Source: Malba Tahan (Júlio César de Mello e Souza), “O Homem que Calculava”, Rio de Janeiro 1938, chapter III. In English: “The Man Who Counted”. An older version with 17 camels can be found in many puzzle books.

LOOKING BACKTHE ESSENTIALS AT A GLANCE

ORDER

Brackets, then multiplication and division before addition and subtraction, otherwise from left to right

$\tfrac12 + \tfrac13 \cdot \tfrac34 = \tfrac12 + \tfrac14 = \tfrac34$

LAWS OF ARITHMETIC

Swapping, grouping, distributing

$\tfrac35 \cdot 4 + \tfrac35 \cdot 6 = \tfrac35 \cdot 10 = 6$

EQUATIONS

Inverse operation, trying, checking

$\tfrac95 \cdot a = 1 \Rightarrow a = \tfrac59$

INEQUALITIES

many solutions, in $\mathbb{Q}^+$ often infinitely many

$4 \cdot x < 3$: all $x < \tfrac34$

PLAN FOR SOLVING

understand, represent, calculate, check and answer

The rest, $\tfrac{5}{12}$, is 15, so 36 in all

TESTTWO ROUNDS · INSTANT FEEDBACK
ROUND 1 · WITHOUT A CALCULATOR

$0.5 + 0.3 \cdot 2 = \;?$

$0.5 + 0.6 = 1.1$

$\tfrac34 \cdot 5 + \tfrac34 \cdot 7 = \;?$

$\tfrac34 \cdot 12 = 9$

$\tfrac95 \cdot a = 1$. What is $a$?

$a = 1 : \tfrac95 = \tfrac59$

ROUND 2 · WORD PROBLEMS

Ali gets a third of the marbles, Bea a quarter, Carl the rest of 15. How many marbles were there?

$\tfrac{5}{12}$ is 15, so all of them are $15 : \tfrac{5}{12} = 36$.

A full glass weighs 450 g, half full 290 g. How much does the empty glass weigh?

Half the juice 160 g, all the juice 320 g, glass $450 - 320 = 130$ g.

A trail is $12.6$ km long. How far is it still when $\tfrac23$ has been done?

$12.6 : 3 = 4.2$ km
